transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Vega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood), Liam O'Connor (CloudArc), Sana Rahman (CloudArc PM), Diego Marquez (CloudArc Infra), Rachel Kim (CloudArc Security), Avery (CloudArc notes)

Summary:
A focused technical sync on publishing CloudArc's joint solution to cloud vendor catalogs and the operational runbook for that listing + hybrid connector. Goals: finalize the ops runbook outline, align on VPC/KMS constraints, decide fallback policies for listing failover, and schedule pilot benchmarks. Action items assigned. Some jargon got mangled in places (BPC for VPC, KFS for KV cache).

Topics Covered:
- Catalog publish checklist and gating criteria
- Network/topology and KMS requirements for listing (VPC vs public endpoints)
- Onboarding runbook: install, config, rollback, monitoring hooks
- Joint pilot: benchmark plan (latency/cost/throughput) and tenants for dedicated vs hosted
- Security questions: audit logs, SOC2 scope, encryption at rest/in transit

Transcript body (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick round robin — can folks say who they are?
[00:08] Liam (CloudArc): Hi, Liam O'Connor from CloudArc, I run partnerships.
[00:12] Sana: Sana, platform product manager.
[00:14] Diego: Diego, infra.
[00:16] Rachel: Rachel in security.
[00:18] Maya: Awesome. Jonas and Priya from my side. We'll run through the publish checklist and then get into the ops runbook.
[00:27] Jonas (Redwood SE): Cool, I have the rough runbook notes open. First callout: are you aiming for a marketplace listing behind a VPC connector or public listing with private data connectors?
[00:36] Diego: We prefer VPC connector for production, we need KMS inside our tenant and can't route model calls over public endpoints for regulated workloads.
[00:44] Rachel: Yep, we have PCI-ish controls, plus we've got customers in EU who need data residency assurance.
[00:51] Maya: Good, that matches typical dedicated/private deployment patterns. For marketplace listing, there are two flows: listing manifest + images, and the back-channel for provisioning the VPC connector. We'll need a small onboarding agent or terraform module.
[01:05] Liam: Terraform is better for our ops team. We already have a TF module for other connectors.
[01:09] Priya (Redwood): Also we can offer a helm chart if you run on-prem — sometimes customers prefer that.
[01:14] Diego: We might want both; helm for onprem pilot, terraform for cloud marketplace.
[01:20] Jonas: Great. On the runbook side, I'm proposing sections: pre-reqs, network layout, KMS integration, install flow, test harness (smoke & benchmarking), rollback steps, monitoring/alerts and runbook playbooks.
[01:34] Maya: That sounds good. Diego, can you share the subnet/CIDR ranges expected for the connector?
[01:39] Diego: Yeah I'll export that after the call.
[01:42] [timestamp note: 01:42 - minor audio artifact, speaker label jumped to Speaker 2 briefly]
[01:50] Rachel: On KMS, we use AWS KMS with external key policy, we don't use cloud-provider-managed keys for all tenants. We may need a passthrough or customer-managed key rotation notes.
[02:02] Jonas: Understood. We'll add an appendix for KMS provider patterns — AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS — include policies and sample IAM statements.
[02:12] Sana: Also two operational constraints: 1) we need full audit logs pushed to our SIEM for the listing provisioning events, and 2) we need token rotation every 30 days.
[02:24] Maya: Good callouts — we can expose the audit log hook to push to your S3 or an HTTP endpoint. Token rotation we can put into the runbook and also offer the API to rotate.
[02:36] Liam: On the marketplace listing metadata, question about supported model variants. We plan to list Redwood-verified model variants and a lightweight quantized variant for low-cost. Any pitfalls?
[02:49] Jonas: The main pitfall is ensuring the marketplace manifest includes the compatible model tag and the fallback policy. For example, if a quantized variant fails under load we want automatic fallback to the higher-precision variant or dedicated capacity.
[03:02] Diego: How does the fallback work network-wise — will it trigger a new VPC connection?
[03:06] Priya: No, fallback is at the routing layer in Redwood: same ingress, switch model variant internally. No new VPC provisioning is required.
[03:14] Diego: Phew, that was my worry — didn't want to recreate tunnels mid-flight.
[03:18] [03:18] Maya: Let's talk about the pilot plan — we recommend a three-phase pilot: onboarding + smoke, small benchmark (latency/95/99 + cost per token), then a production-ish soak with a subset of customers.
[03:33] Liam: Timeline wise we want to be live in the marketplace by mid-June. Is that realistic?
[03:38] Jonas: If we get the runbook and VPC details this week, and the Terraform module by next week, mid-June is plausible. We usually need ~4 weeks of integration work plus a 2-week UAT.
[03:50] Rachel: We'll need to see SOC2 coverage and the audit docs before any production roll.
[03:55] Maya: We'll attach our security pack and SOC2 summary after the call.
[04:00] Sana: One more question on observability — what's the level of per-tenant telemetry we can surface? We need token-level cost/latency breakdowns in the console for billing reconciliation.
[04:12] Priya: We produce token-level usage and latency traces; we can provide access via API or push to your telemetry. For marketplace billing, we can map usage to your account id in the manifest.
[04:26] Diego: For networking, do you support private endpoints or only NAT egress? We need private endpoint to avoid public egress.
[04:33] Jonas: We support private endpoints for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted listing we can do a customer VPC peering or a private connector based on vendor marketplace. There might be limits depending on the cloud marketplace provider.
[04:47] Liam: Ok, let's capture that as an open item — vendor-specific connector capabilities.
[04:51] Maya: Noted.
[04:55] [05:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[05:05] Maya: Back to the runbook, I'm going to read the high-level steps so we all align: Pre-req validation (network, KMS, roles), provisioning (TF apply or helm), smoke tests (API ping, auth), benchmark harness run, rollback (terraform destroy + cleanup script), monitoring hooks (audit, metrics), escalation contacts.
[05:25] Liam: That covers it. On rollback, we want an explicit canary window and automated reversion if error rates spike above threshold.
[05:34] Jonas: We can add automated monitoring policies that trigger an automated rollback or route to fallback model. The runbook will show thresholds and commands.
[05:45] Rachel: For compliance, we need a documented chain of custody for telemetry and logs for at least 12 months.
[05:54] Maya: We'll add retention and export steps to the appendix.
[06:00] Jonas: Quick note: some words in our notes get mangled — the auto transcript sometimes turns VPC into BPC or KV cache into KFS. We'll try to be explicit in the runbook.
[06:12] Diego: Ha, yes please.
[06:15] Maya: Let's jump into the manifest itself. Priya, can you run through required fields?
[06:20] Priya: Sure. At minimum: product name, description, supported regions, images/artifacts, terraform/helm artifact link, network requirements (CIDs, allowed ports), KMS patterns, SLA tiers, contact emails, and marketplace tags (e.g., 'private-deploy', 'dedicated-ready'). Also a post-install script hook name.
[06:41] Liam: For regions we need EU-West, US-East, and APAC-Southeast initially.
[06:47] Priya: Noted. We should also include resource sizing guidance for benchmark targets — e.g., X GPUs for Y qps depending on model variant.
[06:58] Jonas: I'll put sample sizing: for the quantized variant, 1xA10 per n tenants? We'll refine with benchmark numbers.
[07:06] Sana: Can we define success criteria for the pilot — say p95 < 750ms for small prompt, cost below $0.015/token on average for the quantized path?
[07:18] Maya: Solid idea. We'll include acceptance criteria: functional, perf, security.
[07:24] Diego: On metrics collection for perf, what tracing do you inject? OpenTelemetry or custom?
[07:29] Priya: We support OpenTelemetry and can provide a sidecar collector config. We also send Redwood-specific tokens for correlation.
[07:38] Rachel: Make sure the tokens don't include PII. We'll need redactions on any user-prompt samples in logs.
[07:45] Jonas: We have a redaction filter module; we'll list it in the runbook.
[07:50] [08:00] Maya: Alright, moving to the rollback choreography — Diego, what's your preference, immediate destroy vs scale down?
[08:06] Diego: Prefer scale down + preserve logs for postmortem; destroy only after confirmation.
[08:12] Jonas: Runbook will show both: a safe rollback (scale-down, route traffic away) and a hard rollback (destroy infra) with checklists.
[08:22] Sana: Also include a customer notification template for planned and unplanned rollbacks.
[08:28] Maya: Good.
[08:30] [08:30] Jonas: I want to flag one technical deep-dive item for follow-up — KV cache invalidation semantics across model variants. If we fallback model to a different architecture, do we need to invalidate KV cache?
[08:44] Diego: That matters for correctness yes.
[08:47] Priya: Short answer — depends on model family. We'll create a mapping in the runbook: compatible variants share KV caches; incompatible ones cause a cache warm-up and we'll document expected latency hit.
[08:59] Maya: We'll put that in the appendix.
[09:02] Liam: Any vendor approvals needed for private connector? Some marketplaces require security review.
[09:08] Rachel: We'll need a checklist of required docs and an owner for vendor security questions.
[09:13] Maya: Redwood will provide the security pack; CloudArc to lead vendor paperwork.
[09:18] Jonas: Ok, quick check — are there any blockers preventing the Terraform module from being used?
[09:23] Diego: We have an internal policy about third-party modules; we might have to mirror the module into our private registry and run an SCA scan.
[09:31] Priya: We can publish the module as a reference and you can import it into your private registry; we'll note SCA steps.
[09:37] Liam: Sounds fine.
[09:40] [09:40] Maya: Time check — we have about 45 minutes left. Let's go through specific doc owners and dates. Jonas, you'll take runbook draft. Priya, you'll produce the manifest template and terraform/helm snippets. Diego and Rachel will provide network and KMS details respectively. Liam and Sana will coordinate pilot calendar.
[09:56] Jonas: I'll aim to have the runbook draft end of week (2026-04-28).
[10:00] Priya: Manifest template and snippets by 2026-04-25.
[10:04] Diego: We'll share network diagrams and VPC details by 2026-05-04.
[10:08] Rachel: Security notes and KMS provider confirmation by 2026-05-04.
[10:12] Liam: Pilot window proposal by 2026-05-01.
[10:15] Maya: Great.
[10:18] [10:18] Speaker 3: (brief echo)
[10:20] Sana: One more small item — licensing terms. If we list on the marketplace, do you handle metered billing or is that through CloudArc?
[10:30] Maya: For marketplace we'll support metered billing integration — Redwood reports usage tied to the manifest account id and the marketplace can invoice. We can also support a pass-through where CloudArc invoices. We'll surface pros/cons in the docs.
[10:43] Liam: Keep both options.
[10:44] Jonas: Competitor note — ApexAI has a similar listing but they're missing the private connector offering; CloudFlow bundles billing which complicates vendor fees. We'll include differentiation notes.
[10:59] Maya: Anything else?
[11:01] Diego: On benchmarking, can Redwood run an initial bench on a Redwood dedicated pool so we get baseline numbers?
[11:07] Jonas: Yes we can provision a small dedicated run bench — we'll need expected QPS, payload sizes and prompt distribution.
[11:13] Diego: I'll send a sample workload file.
[11:16] Maya: Perfect. Last bit — recap and next steps.
[11:20] Maya: Recap: Jonas to share runbook draft by 4/28; Priya manifest by 4/25; CloudArc to share network/KMS by 5/4; Redwood to attach security pack; schedule pilot gating call for week of 5/11. Action items captured in the doc.
[11:36] Liam: Thanks all.
[11:37] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the repo and draft docs.
[11:41] [End of recording]
